text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister says investment projects worth 29.7 million went into the production of goods in order to boost Egypt's export capabilities.
- Ministerial committee for privatisation to determine prices of shares of 11 companies to be sold to the public through the stock exchange.
- Parliament to discuss at next session draft law for owners of buildings.
- Foreign Minister Moussa met with U.S. ambassador to Cairo and talked by telephone with U.S. envoy Dennis Ross. Albright receives encouraging reports from peace coordinator.
- Health Ministry to remain responsible for registering and pricing medicines.
- Central Bank monthly report says inflation down to 4.9 percent at the end of May.
- Interior minister challenges al-Shaab newspaper to offer single document as proof of its lies about corruption among officials.
- IMF representative in Eygpt says international financial institutions have begun to direct some of their money away from Asian and Latin American markets towards Egypt.
- Twenty international petroleum companies have come forward to buy special information on new exploration sites in Egypt.
- Central Bank governor says Egypt's foreign currency reserves up to 20.199 billion pounds from 19.746 billion.
- Heavy rain caused Egypt Air plane to skid off runway in Istanbul.
